idiom_name: enum class with constructor data (+ entries / when exhaustiveness)
implementation_notes: Kotlin's enum class is a nominal closed set: constants live in the enum's namespace, carry constructor data and methods, and are accessible through entries (Kotlin 1.9+, an EnumEntries list) instead of the allocating values(). A when over an enum used as an expression must be exhaustive, so adding a member fails compilation at every decision site - the compiler-enforced form of the pattern's closure. A sealed interface is the sibling realization when cases need different payloads; that is the algebraic data type decision, not this one.
pitfalls: values() allocates a fresh array on every call - iterate entries (Kotlin 1.9+) or enumEntries() instead.
ordinal is declaration order and participates in compareTo; never persist it.
Adding an entry breaks every non-else when expression (deliberate, but budget for the migration); ordinal-based APIs such as EnumSet-like helpers do not exist in the stdlib.
